1//! Parse `format!`-like strings. This is mostly useful if you want to write a proc
2//! macro and want to implement `format!`-like functionality without relying on the
3//! original macro.
4//!
5//! See <https://github.com/CombiRWTH/graph-visualiser-website/blob/6dcce28567d08bb73d4b2bd7533bf246291f3a76/rust/algorithm/impl/src/lib.rs#L203-L223>
6//! for an example usage of this crate.

11use chumsky::{
12	prelude::*,
13	text::{self, whitespace}
14};
15use std::{borrow::Cow, fmt::Debug, str::FromStr};
16
17/// A parser for an unsigned integer.
18fn uint<'a, T>(radix: u32) -> impl Parser<'a, &'a str, T> + Clone
19where
20	T: FromStr,
21	T::Err: Debug
22{
23	text::int(radix).map(|s: &str| s.parse().unwrap())
24}
25
26fn is_relaxed(ch: &char) -> bool {
27	!ch.is_whitespace() && !ch.is_control() && *ch != ':' && *ch != '{' && *ch != '}'
28}
29
30/// A parser for an identifier. This can be either chumsky's `text::ident` parser which
31/// parses any C-style identifier, or a relaxed identifier.
32///
33/// A relaxed identifier doesn't start with a numeric character and contains any
34/// characters that are
35///  - not control chars
36///  - not a whitespace
37///  - not a colon (`:`)
38///  - no braces (`{` or `}`)
39fn ident<'a>(relaxed: bool) -> impl Parser<'a, &'a str, Cow<'a, str>> + Clone {
40	if relaxed {
41		any()
42			.filter(|ch: &char| is_relaxed(ch) && !ch.is_numeric())
43			.then(any().filter(is_relaxed).repeated().to_slice())
44			.map(|(first, chars)| format!("{first}{chars}").into())
45			.boxed()
46	} else {
47		text::ident().map(Into::into).boxed()
48	}
49}

51/// A variable name. This can be one of these 3 cases:
52///
53///  - `{}` is [`VarName::None`]
54///  - `{1}` is [`VarName::Index(1)`]
55///  - `{foo}` is [`VarName::Ident("foo")`]
56#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
57pub enum VarName {
58	None,
59	Index(usize),
60	Ident(String)
61}
62
63impl VarName {
64	fn parser<'a>(relaxed: bool) -> impl Parser<'a, &'a str, Self> + Clone {
65		choice((
66			uint(10).map(Self::Index),
67			ident(relaxed).map(|ident| Self::Ident(ident.into_owned())),
68			empty().map(|_| Self::None)
69		))
70	}
71}
72
73/// A parameter to an option. Can be either a constant or dependent on a variable.
74#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
75pub enum Param {
76	Const(usize),
77	Dynamic(VarName)
78}
79
80#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
81pub enum Align {
82	Left,
83	Center,
84	Right
85}
86
87impl Align {
88	fn parser<'a>() -> impl Parser<'a, &'a str, Self> + Clone {
89		choice((
90			just("<").map(|_| Self::Left),
91			just("^").map(|_| Self::Center),
92			just(">").map(|_| Self::Right),
93			empty().map(|_| Self::Left)
94		))
95	}
96}
97
98#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
99pub enum Padding {
100	/// Padding with zeroes. Usually for numbers.
101	ZeroPadding { width: usize },
102
103	/// Padding a custom char. Using spaces by default.
104	TextPadding {
105		ch: char,
106		align: Align,
107		width: Param
108	}
109}
110
111impl Padding {
112	fn zero_padding_parser<'a>() -> impl Parser<'a, &'a str, Self> + Clone {
113		just("0")
114			.ignore_then(uint(10))
115			.map(|width| Self::ZeroPadding { width })
116	}
117
118	fn text_padding_parser<'a>() -> impl Parser<'a, &'a str, Self> + Clone {
119		let width_parser = choice((
120			uint(10)
121				.then_ignore(just("$"))
122				.map(|idx| Param::Dynamic(VarName::Index(idx))),
123			ident(false)
124				.then_ignore(just("$"))
125				.map(|name| Param::Dynamic(VarName::Ident(name.into_owned()))),
126			uint(10).map(Param::Const)
127		));
128
129		// we need two parsers here, otherwise the any() would parse the token that
130		// specifies the alignment if only the alignment is specified
131		choice((
132			empty()
133				.map(|_| ' ')
134				.then(Align::parser())
135				.then(width_parser.clone()),
136			any().then(Align::parser()).then(width_parser)
137		))
138		.map(|((ch, align), width)| Self::TextPadding { ch, align, width })
139	}
140}

142#[derive(Clone, Copy, Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
143pub enum Style {
144	Display,
145	Debug,
146	LowerHex,
147	UpperHex,
148	Binary,
149	Octal
150}
151
152impl Style {
153	fn parser<'a>() -> impl Parser<'a, &'a str, Self> + Clone {
154		choice((
155			just("?").map(|_| Self::Debug),
156			just("x").map(|_| Self::LowerHex),
157			just("X").map(|_| Self::UpperHex),
158			just("b").map(|_| Self::Binary),
159			just("o").map(|_| Self::Octal),
160			empty().map(|_| Self::Display)
161		))
162	}
163}

165#[derive(Debug, Eq, PartialEq)]
166pub enum Token {
167	/// A text token. Double braces (`{{` and `}}`) have already been converted to single
168	/// braces.
169	Text(String),
170
171	/// A variable/placeholder.
172	Variable {
173		/// The name of the variable. Can be empty, an index, or an ident.
174		name: VarName,
175
176		/// The padding/fill/alignment of the variable.
177		padding: Option<Padding>,
178		/// The precision of the argument.
179		precision: Option<Param>,
180
181		/// The style of the variable.
182		style: Style,
183		/// Whether to use pretty printing (`{:#}`).
184		pretty: bool,
185		/// Whether to print signs (`{:+}`).
186		sign: bool
187	}
188}
189
190impl Token {
191	fn parser<'a>(relaxed: bool) -> impl Parser<'a, &'a str, Self> + Clone {
192		// a parser that parses text occurences and unescapes {{ and }} while parsing
193		let text_parser = none_of("{}")
194			.or(just("{{").map(|_| '{'))
195			.or(just("}}").map(|_| '}'))
196			.repeated()
197			.at_least(1)
198			.collect::<String>()
199			.map(Self::Text);
200
201		// a parser that parses simple variables consisting only of braces and name
202		let simple_var_parser = just("{")
203			.ignore_then(VarName::parser(relaxed))
204			.then_ignore(whitespace())
205			.then_ignore(just("}"))
206			.map(|name| Self::Variable {
207				name,
208				padding: None,
209				precision: None,
210				style: Style::Display,
211				pretty: false,
212				sign: false
213			});
214
215		// a parser that parses the precision option of variables
216		let precision_parser = just(".")
217			.ignore_then(choice((
218				uint(10)
219					.then_ignore(just("$"))
220					.map(|idx| Param::Dynamic(VarName::Index(idx))),
221				ident(false)
222					.then_ignore(just("$"))
223					.map(|ident| Param::Dynamic(VarName::Ident(ident.into_owned()))),
224				just("*").map(|_| Param::Dynamic(VarName::None)),
225				uint(10).map(Param::Const)
226			)))
227			.map(Some)
228			.or(empty().map(|_| None));
229
230		// a parser for variables that might have text padding but no zero padding
231		let text_padding_parser = just("{")
232			.ignore_then(VarName::parser(relaxed))
233			.then_ignore(just(":"))
234			.then(
235				Padding::text_padding_parser()
236					.map(Some)
237					.or(empty().map(|_| None))
238			)
239			.then(just("+").map(|_| true).or(empty().map(|_| false)))
240			.then(just("#").map(|_| true).or(empty().map(|_| false)))
241			.then(precision_parser.clone())
242			.then(Style::parser())
243			.then_ignore(whitespace())
244			.then_ignore(just("}"))
245			.map(|(((((name, padding), sign), pretty), precision), style)| {
246				Self::Variable {
247					name,
248					padding,
249					precision,
250					style,
251					pretty,
252					sign
253				}
254			});
255
256		// a parser for variables that might have zero padding but no text padding
257		let zero_padding_parser = just("{")
258			.ignore_then(VarName::parser(relaxed))
259			.then_ignore(just(":"))
260			.then(just("+").map(|_| true).or(empty().map(|_| false)))
261			.then(just("#").map(|_| true).or(empty().map(|_| false)))
262			.then(
263				Padding::zero_padding_parser()
264					.map(Some)
265					.or(empty().map(|_| None))
266			)
267			.then(precision_parser)
268			.then(Style::parser())
269			.then_ignore(whitespace())
270			.then_ignore(just("}"))
271			.map(|(((((name, sign), pretty), padding), precision), style)| {
272				Self::Variable {
273					name,
274					padding,
275					precision,
276					style,
277					pretty,
278					sign
279				}
280			});
281
282		choice((
283			text_parser,
284			simple_var_parser,
285			text_padding_parser,
286			zero_padding_parser
287		))
288	}
289}
290
291/// Parse a format string. This should mimic the behaviour of Rust. All deviations (both
292/// inputs accepted by Rust but not this function and vice versa) are considered bugs.
293pub fn parse(input: &str) -> ParseResult<Vec<Token>, EmptyErr> {
294	Token::parser(false)
295		.repeated()
296		.collect()
297		.then_ignore(end())
298		.parse(input)
299}
300
301/// Parse a format string with relaxed idents. Only the initial identifier of a variable
302/// is relaxed,
303///
304/// A relaxed identifier doesn't start with a numeric character and contains any
305/// characters that are
306///  - not control chars
307///  - not a whitespace
308///  - not a colon (`:`)
309///  - no braces (`{` or `}`)
310pub fn parse_relaxed(input: &str) -> ParseResult<Vec<Token>, EmptyErr> {
311	Token::parser(true)
312		.repeated()
313		.collect()
314		.then_ignore(end())
315		.parse(input)
316}
